title: Customer Care Training Note — How Many Warranty Coverage Registrations a Customer Holds
content:
**Rule.** Under Warranty Coverage, a customer holds one registration for every completed contract, so a homeowner with a window contract and a door contract holds two registrations, each with its own plan. A contract's products have only one registration in force at a time; a transfer closes the seller's registration as transferred before the buyer's registration is issued. The number of registrations a customer holds is not capped.

## What the records must show

- A registration is tied to the contract it covers: a window contract, or a door contract.
- "In force" means a registration whose status is active or transfer pending.
- For any one contract, the registration records show at most one registration in force. The registration number on each certificate is distinct.
- Whether a contract already has a registration in force is read from the system's registration records for that contract, not from what the customer says.

## The rule in other forms

| Situation on the records | Registrations the customer holds |
|---|---|
| One completed window contract | one, under that contract's plan |
| One completed window contract and one completed door contract | two, each under its own plan |
| Several completed contracts | one per completed contract, with no upper limit |

The order on a transfer: the seller's registration is closed as transferred first, and the buyer's registration for the same contract is issued after it, so the contract never has two registrations in force at once.

## Questions answered

**A homeowner has a Ridgeline window contract under one plan and a Ridgeline door contract under another. Is there one combined Warranty Coverage?** No. There are two registrations, each with its own plan.

**Is there a ceiling on how many registrations one customer may hold?** No. The number is not capped.

**When a home is sold and the coverage passes to the buyer, can both registrations be in force together?** No. The seller's registration becomes transferred before the buyer's is issued.
